name: approval
title: Approval
purpose: One request from an agent that waits for the reader's answer: what would run, where, for whom and why, with Allow and Decline.
whenToUse: When an agent is blocked until the reader allows or declines a tool call or a command.
Alone in a view for one request, or as list items in a queue of several.
whenNotToUse: For a request that was already answered or denied. Use a message row in the transcript.
To say how many requests wait. Use the pending tray.
To confirm an action the reader started themselves, such as deleting a workspace. Use a dialog.

variants.name: normal
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. The risk line is optional. When it is shown it reads Normal risk and what keeps it so, beside an info icon.

variants.name: elevated
variants.use: A request that reaches outside the task's worktree, deletes, or cannot be undone. The risk line reads Elevated risk and why, beside a warning icon, on a tinted band.

accessibility: Use an article with aria-labelledby pointing at gw-approval__title, a heading. The title says who asks and for what. Its level is the one under the heading it sits beneath: h2 directly under the view's h1, h3 inside a section headed by an h2. In a queue or a list every title takes the same level. The class sets the size, so the level changes nothing on screen. The examples use h4 only because of where they sit on the gallery page.

Emphasis: when a view shows a single approval, Allow may be the view's primary action, gw-button gw-button--primary. When approvals are listed, each card sits in its own li of a ul and Allow is a plain gw-button, never primary, so a queue has no competing primary actions.

Allow comes first and Decline sits at the far end of gw-approval__actions. Both are always visible, carry data-gw-critical so the checker can see they are never hidden, and are never placed inside a details element.

The risk line, gw-approval__risk, is optional. Leave it out when the app does not grade requests, and never write one the app cannot back with a reason. When it is shown, it comes first in the card, starts with the words Normal risk or Elevated risk and then says why. Its icon is drawn by the stylesheet, so the tone is never colour alone. An elevated request always has its risk line.
gw-approval__command holds exactly what would run, as text, with characters that cannot be seen written out. It wraps, and never scrolls sideways.
Supporting detail goes in a details element with a text summary, such as Show the full request. It holds no control the reader needs in order to answer.

A note on declining is optional. Before the actions, add a details element whose summary reads Add a note for the agent, holding gw-approval__note with one labelled field and no button. It starts closed, without the open attribute. The card has one Decline button, and it sends whatever note has been typed: nothing when the field is empty or was never opened. Never add a second decline button, because a reader who types a note and presses the plain Decline would lose it. Allow does not send the note, and the field's label says so.

While the answer is sent, set aria-busy="true" on the pressed button, change its label to Allowing or Declining, and disable the other. If sending fails, restore both and add gw-approval__error with role="alert", saying that nothing was allowed.

Tab reaches each summary, the note field when it is open, then Allow, then Decline. Enter and Space activate each. The component needs no script: the app sets aria-busy and disabled, and removes the card once the request is answered. Move focus to the next card or the view's heading when it goes.
